implementation: Preserve direct native scenario/map LFG lookup first. If absent, obtain the native default map difficulty and shared team-eligible LFG metadata, then resolve ObjectMgr's actual map/difficulty/team/class/dungeon route. Accept only the requested scenario and matching nonzero route restrictions; zero fields retain native wildcard semantics.

Use the same resolver for login admission and legacy entrance initialization. Keep existing current-boot/live-map/scenario/instance/completion checks, old-boot entrance restart, selector consumption and checkpoint persistence unchanged. No scenario/map whitelist, invented DB2/LFG row, character progress reset or schema migration.

Extend extracted production handler tests with shared-route fresh/live/legacy entrance positives, missing metadata/route negatives, wrong scenario/team/class/difficulty/dungeon rejection, wildcard admission and exact-route precedence.

Extend actual serialized-packet tests with complete logout/login. Move each scratch Player eight yards through native Map::PlayerRelocation before saving, keeping the recorded entrance distinct from the later position. Live rejoining must preserve that later position and native stage1/partial criteria; an old-boot checkpoint must use a different native instance at entrance/stage0 with no old criteria.

native_modes.live_early: A current-boot checkpoint rejoins the same live Scenario. Loading finish before the99+1ms admission callback queues no early initialization; admitted initialization has native scenario ID, current step, ActiveSteps and full criteria progress.
native_modes.live_late: Same native save/load/rejoin path, with loading finish after map admission. Initialization is withheld until finish and sent once.
native_modes.old_boot_early: After another real save/logout, change only the scratch checkpoint's boot value. Even though its old native instance is still alive, full login allocates a new instance at the recorded entrance and emits stage0 after early finish/admission.
native_modes.old_boot_late: Same old-boot restart with finish after admission. No stale stage/criteria or extra initialization.

native_data.routing: Native LFG908 references786; world scenario_data selects786 for team469 and1189 for team67, with class/difficulty/LFG wildcard fields. Full native load uses these actual stores and routes; tests do not supply fake LFG metadata or a fake Scenario.

method_and_limits: 64 complete relog cases:32 current-boot live and32 old-boot restarts, evenly split across both factions and early/late loading finishes. Four parent raid-difficulty contexts and two parent travel directions repeat the faction cases. The prior48 actual scenario initialization/fresh teleport cases remain in the same run.

Criteria progress is created by real type92 events, including actual stage advancement and7/33 accumulation. The fixture does not write Scenario stage/progress internals. Native SaveToDB/LogoutPlayer, persisted checkpoint parsing, accepted login/socket/SQL callback, actual map factory/admission, actual serialization and original final-link libraries are exercised.

The old-boot cases deliberately alter only a disposable checkpoint's boot value after a real save, while keeping the old native instance alive. This tests boot separation and entrance restart; it is not an observed process restart, crash recovery or actor-state serialization. Native PlayerRelocation establishes distinct positions for persistence checks and is not a test of client movement/collision.

Extracted negative routing tests execute the production resolver against controlled metadata boundaries. Native positive cases use runtime DB2/world metadata. Existing direct routes retain their prior precedence; this change does not redesign ObjectMgr/LFG selection globally.

No WoW client was operated. Actual UI, encrypted packet delivery, scene/voice/quest actor traversal, camera, pet portrait and full Broken Shore completion remain client checks. Fixture-owned map workers are stopped for deterministic lifecycle tests; arbitrary thread interleavings are not established.
Only schema-only disposable character/auth databases and scratch characters are written. World access is read-only; personal rows, runtime configuration and extracted data are preserved.
